scenes.say: Caching can cut load times and save costs, but which strategy should you use?

scenes.label: Cache-aside
scenes.sub: App loads data into cache only when needed.
scenes.say: Cache-aside means your app grabs data from the cache when it’s there, or loads it from the database if it’s not.
Cache-aside works well for read-heavy workloads. Write-through keeps cache and database synced, but can slow down writes.
Set time-to-live to expire cache keys. Use invalidation to clear outdated data. CDNs cache content closer to users for speed.

scenes.question: What happens on a cache miss?
scenes.right: Read from database, store in cache, return to user.
scenes.say: If you miss in the cache, don’t just fail. Fetch from the database, update the cache, and send the data back.
